stories.headline: Meta planning sweeping layoffs of 20% workforce as AI infrastructure costs mount

key_facts.fact: Meta is planning layoffs that could affect 20% or more of its nearly 79,000-person workforce — roughly 16,000 jobs — to offset costly AI infrastructure bets.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta is considering major layoffs that could affect 20% or more of the company's workforce, according to Reuters. Meta employed nearly 79,000 people as of December 31, according to a recent filing.

key_facts.fact: Top executives recently signaled the plans to senior leaders and told them to begin planning cutbacks; layoffs could begin within a month, though timing and magnitude are not finalized.
key_facts.excerpt: Two senior employees familiar with the plans reportedly told Business Insider that the layoffs could begin in a month.

key_facts.fact: Meta plans to spend approximately $600 billion on AI infrastructure and data centers by 2028 and has spent hundreds of millions to attract AI researchers to its superintelligence team.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta has previously said it plans to pour approximately $600 billion into new AI infrastructure and data centers by 2028, a necessary investment for its AI ambitions.

key_facts.fact: CEO Mark Zuckerberg said on a January earnings call that the company was 'elevating individual contributors and flattening teams' and that 'projects that used to require big teams now be accomplished by a single, very talented person.'
key_facts.excerpt: During a January earnings call, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg told investors that the company was 'elevating individual contributors and flattening teams.' He also said that he is now seeing 'projects that used to require big teams now be accomplished by a single, very talented person.'

key_facts.fact: A Meta spokesperson called the report 'speculative reporting about theoretical approaches,' and some pundits including OpenAI's Sam Altman have suggested many tech layoffs are 'AI-washing' where executives use AI as cover for other issues.
key_facts.excerpt: 'This is speculative reporting about theoretical approaches,' a Meta spokesperson said. Some pundits, and even executives like OpenAI's Sam Altman, have suggested that many of these cuts are 'AI-washing,' where executives use AI as cover for other issues.

key_facts.fact: If confirmed, the layoffs would be Meta's largest restructuring since November 2022 when it cut 11,000 jobs, followed by another 10,000 in March 2023.
key_facts.excerpt: The last time Meta announced layoffs of this scale was in November 2022, when it cut 11,000 jobs, followed by another 10,000 in March 2023.

stories.headline: Elon Musk confirms Tesla Terafab AI chip factory launches in 7 days

key_facts.fact: On March 14, Elon Musk posted on X that the Terafab Project launches in seven days, setting the launch date for approximately March 21, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: On March 14, Elon Musk posted on X that the Terafab Project launches in seven days.

key_facts.fact: The Terafab facility is designed to produce between 100 and 200 billion custom AI and memory chips per year, targeting an initial output of 100,000 wafer starts per month with ambitions to scale toward one million.
key_facts.excerpt: The facility is designed to produce between 100 and 200 billion custom AI and memory chips per year, targeting an initial output of 100,000 wafer starts per month with a stated ambition to scale toward one million.

key_facts.fact: The project carries an estimated cost of approximately $25 billion, forming part of Tesla's record capital expenditure plan for 2026 which exceeds $20 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: The project carries an estimated cost of approximately $25 billion, forming part of Tesla's record capital expenditure plan for 2026, which exceeds $20 billion.

key_facts.fact: Tesla is designing its fifth-generation AI chip (AI5) to power autonomous driving systems including Full Self-Driving, and currently partners with TSMC and Samsung for chip fabrication.
key_facts.excerpt: Tesla is designing its fifth-generation AI chip to power its autonomous ambitions. Musk reaffirmed that Tesla was also partnering with Taiwan's TSMC and South Korea's Samsung.

key_facts.fact: Musk warned at last year's shareholder meeting that even the most optimistic scenario for supplier chip output would be insufficient, characterizing Terafab as 'the only viable path' to meet Tesla's target chip volume.
key_facts.excerpt: Musk told investors the company needs to build a chip fabrication facility to avoid a supply constraint it projects will materialise within three to four years.

key_facts.fact: The facility would combine logic processing, memory storage, and advanced packaging under one roof — vertically integrated chip manufacturing on a scale no private company outside Taiwan and South Korea currently operates.
key_facts.excerpt: The facility would combine logic processing, memory storage, and advanced packaging under one roof — vertically integrated chip manufacturing on a scale no private company outside Taiwan and South Korea currently operates.

stories.headline: Nvidia GTC 2026 opens in San Jose with 30,000+ attendees and agentic AI focus

key_facts.fact: Nvidia GTC 2026 opened on March 15 at the San Jose Convention Center with full-day technical workshops on multimodal AI agents, end-to-end robotics workflows, and accelerated networking for AI infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA GTC begins today at the San Jose Convention Center with full-day technical workshops on topics including multimodal AI agents, end-to-end robotics workflows and accelerated networking for AI infrastructure.

key_facts.fact: More than 30,000 attendees from 190+ countries are expected, with Jensen Huang's keynote scheduled for March 16 at 11 a.m. PT at the SAP Center.
key_facts.excerpt: Tomorrow, thousands of attendees will pack the SAP Center for the keynote address by NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang at 11 a.m. PT.

key_facts.fact: The conference's central theme is the shift from training-era AI to inference and agentic AI, with the Vera Rubin GPU architecture (successor to Blackwell) expected to be formally showcased, featuring up to 288GB of HBM4 memory.
key_facts.excerpt: The overarching theme is agentic AI—autonomous systems that act, not just answer. Early specifications point to up to 288GB of HBM4 memory per unit—a substantial jump from Blackwell's configurations.

key_facts.fact: NemoClaw, Nvidia's entry into the agent platform market, is expected to be announced, alongside details of a Groq licensing deal for low-latency inference tasks.
key_facts.excerpt: NemoClaw: Nvidia Enters the Agent Platform Market. The Groq licensing deal—announced earlier this week—will also factor in: Groq's chip designs are positioned to handle low-latency inference tasks.

key_facts.fact: The conference features over 1,000 sessions and more than 240 Nvidia Inception startups showcasing technologies across physical AI, robotics, generative AI, and enterprise applications.
key_facts.excerpt: The conference, running from March 16-19, will take place in San Jose, California, at the SAP Center with over 1,000 sessions. There will also be more than 240 Nvidia Inception startups showcasing technologies across physical AI, robotics, generative AI and enterprise applications.

key_facts.fact: A hotly anticipated panel led by Jensen Huang on open source frontier models will feature Perplexity's Aravind Srinivas and Thinking Machines Lab's Mira Murati.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia GTC 2026 is set to be one of the biggest AI conferences of the year, featuring a hotly anticipated panel discussion led by Jensen Huang on the state of open source frontier models, with participants including Perplexity's Aravind Srinivas and Thinking Machines Lab's Mira Murati.

stories.headline: ACE Robotics open-sources Kairos 3.0-4B, embodied AI world model 72x faster than Cosmos

key_facts.fact: ACE Robotics open-sourced Kairos 3.0-4B, described as the industry's first native world model for embodied intelligence with unified multi-modal understanding, generation, and prediction in a single architecture.
key_facts.excerpt: ACE ROBOTICS announced the open-source release of Kairos 3.0-4B, the industry's first native world model for embodied intelligence to realize unified 'multi-modal understanding-generation-prediction' within a single architecture.

key_facts.fact: The 4B-parameter model achieves inference speeds 72 times faster than Nvidia's Cosmos 2.5 on A800 GPUs while requiring only 23.5GB VRAM compared to Cosmos 2.5's 70.2GB.
key_facts.excerpt: Its inference speed is 72 times faster than Cosmos 2.5, setting a new global performance record for embodied world models.

key_facts.fact: Kairos 3.0-4B enables cross-embodiment generalization, allowing a single model to drive robots of multiple form factors including single-arm, dual-arm, and dexterous hand configurations across platforms like Agilex PIPER, Unitree G1, and Galaxy G1.
key_facts.excerpt: A native world model built from the ground up for embodied intelligence, Kairos 3.0-4B delivers exceptional physics-consistent deep understanding and cross-embodiment generalization, enabling a single 'brain' to drive robots of multiple form factors.

key_facts.fact: The model generates coherent interaction videos up to 7 minutes long and achieves 1.5x faster-than-real-time generation speed on the Nvidia Jetson Thor T5000 edge platform.
key_facts.excerpt: It achieves real-time edge generation on the THOR platform with a 1:1.5 ratio of generation time to video duration. 7-minute coherent interaction videos set a new industry benchmark.

key_facts.fact: ACE Robotics was founded by Wang Xiaogang, co-founder of SenseTime, and the startup completed its angel financing round earlier in the week of the release.
key_facts.excerpt: ACE Robotics was founded by Wang Xiaogang, the co-founder of SenseTime in late 2025. The startup completed its angel round of financing earlier this week.

stories.headline: Ai2 releases MolmoSpaces and MolmoBot for zero-shot sim-to-real robot transfer

key_facts.fact: Allen Institute for AI (Ai2) released MolmoSpaces and MolmoBot, open-source robotics models trained exclusively in simulation that work directly on real robots without any manually collected data or fine-tuning.
key_facts.excerpt: Ai2 has released new robotics models trained exclusively in simulations. The models are designed to work directly on real robots without any manually collected data or fine-tuning, what researchers call zero-shot sim-to-real transfer.

key_facts.fact: MolmoSpaces includes over 230,000 indoor scenes, more than 130,000 curated objects, and over 42 million physics-based robotic grasping annotations for training.
key_facts.excerpt: MolmoSpaces includes 'over 230,000 indoor scenes, more than 130,000 curated objects, and over 42 million physics-based robotic grasping annotations.'

key_facts.fact: MolmoBot can execute object manipulation tasks including picking up and placing objects, opening drawers, and operating doors — all without exposure to real-world training data for these specific tasks.
key_facts.excerpt: MolmoBot can execute object manipulation tasks including picking up and placing objects, opening drawers, and operating doors—all without exposure to real-world training data for these specific tasks.

key_facts.fact: The approach could significantly accelerate development: conventional training typically required months of teleoperated real-world demonstrations to make simulation-trained robots reliable.
key_facts.excerpt: The approach could significantly accelerate development: with conventional training, researchers typically needed months of teleoperated real-world demonstrations to make simulation-trained robots reliable.

key_facts.fact: Ranjay Krishna, director of the PRIOR team at Ai2, explains that closing the simulation-reality gap depends on dramatically increasing environmental variety, object diversity, and camera condition variations.
key_facts.excerpt: Ranjay Krishna, director of the PRIOR team at Ai2, explains that closing the simulation-reality gap depends on dramatically increasing environmental variety, object diversity, and camera condition variations.

stories.headline: Lyzr AI raises $14.5M at $250M valuation for enterprise AI agent platform

key_facts.fact: Enterprise AI startup Lyzr AI raised $14.5 million in a Series A+ round led by Accenture with participation from Rocketship VC, valuing the company at $250 million — a fivefold increase from its October valuation.
key_facts.excerpt: Lyzr AI raised $14.5 million in a Series A+ round led by Accenture with participation from Rocketship VC, valuing the company at $250 million. The funding values the New York–based startup at $250 million and represents a fivefold increase from its valuation in October.

key_facts.fact: Lyzr develops full-stack agent infrastructure that enables enterprises to design, deploy, and manage AI agents that automate workflows while maintaining control over sensitive data and internal systems.
key_facts.excerpt: Founded in 2023, the company develops infrastructure that enables enterprises to design, deploy, and manage AI agents that automate workflows while maintaining control over sensitive data and internal systems.

key_facts.fact: The platform uses a multi-agent architecture to improve reliability and transparency and has been adopted by organizations across finance, healthcare, and energy sectors, with revenue growing more than 300% in recent quarters.

stories.headline: AgentMail raises $6M from General Catalyst to build email infrastructure for AI agents

key_facts.fact: AgentMail raised $6 million in seed funding led by General Catalyst with participation from Y Combinator, Phosphor Capital, and several angel investors to build what it describes as the first email provider created for autonomous AI systems.
key_facts.excerpt: AgentMail announced it has raised $6 million in seed funding to build what it describes as the first email provider created for autonomous AI systems. The funding round was led by General Catalyst with participation from Y Combinator, Phosphor Capital, and several angel investors.

key_facts.fact: The platform provides dedicated email inboxes for AI agents, enabling them to communicate with both humans and other systems as autonomous digital workers across industries.
key_facts.excerpt: AgentMail's platform provides dedicated email inboxes designed for agents, enabling them to communicate with both humans and other systems using a familiar internet standard.

key_facts.fact: Founded by University of Michigan graduates Haakam Aujla, Michael Kim, and Adi Singh with experience from Optiver, Nvidia, and Accel, the company addresses the gap in infrastructure for AI agents as they move beyond chat interfaces to handle complex operational tasks.
key_facts.excerpt: AgentMail was founded by University of Michigan graduates Haakam Aujla, Michael (Hyun) Kim, and Adi Singh, whose previous experience includes roles at Optiver, Nvidia, and Accel. The founders said the company is focused on providing the infrastructure needed for AI agents to operate as digital workers across industries.
